name: Rice Gall Midge
description: A small fly whose larvae cause formation of tubular galls (silver shoots) in place of normal rice tillers. It is a serious pest of rice in West Africa, causing yield losses of 20-80% in severe outbreaks.
symptoms: Silver shoots emerging from leaf whorls instead of normal leaves
Stunted plant growth with many non-productive tillers
Galls are longer and lighter green than normal leaves
lifecycle: Larva (crawls to growing point, induces gall)
treatments: Apply systemic insecticides (imidacloprid) at first sign of silver shoots
Spray chlorpyrifos at early tillering stage
Remove and destroy silver shoots to reduce pest population
Use neem-based repellents as preventive spray
prevention: Plant resistant rice varieties (e.g., NERICA gall-midge tolerant lines)
Practice synchronized planting within communities to reduce pest buildup
Avoid continuous rice cropping — rotate with dryland crops
Drain fields for 3-5 days to suppress midge survival
